newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor leader sees 16.5 pct 1997 inflation.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor leader sees 16.5 pct 1997 inflation.

text.p: A Mexican labor leader on Thursday estimated inflation of up to 16.5 percent for 1997, a jump from the government's official target of 15 percent.
Vice-president of the Labor Congress, Enrique Aguilar, told reporters the higher inflation estimate should be taken into consideration when negotiating wage increases.
"Considering what we have been seeing and inflationary indexes from the Banco de Mexico, we could close the year at about 16 or 16.5 percent," Aguilar said.
He suggested salary increases be applied as of January instead of in December. Annual salary revisions in December usually contribute to the seasonal inflation spike that month.
Aguilar added that forthcoming salary rises should be "three or four points above inflation expected for next year."
Commerce Secretary Herminio Blanco said salary and contract negotiations have been smooth in the bimonthly meeting of government, union and business leaders.
He said average wage rises in July were about 19.5 percent, for a purchasing power rise of seven percent.
The consumer price index for the first seven months of the year rose 9.61 percent. Mexico's inflation last year rose 27.7 percent, compared with the government's target of 20.5 percent.
